[s0l0!-header][h1]Functional Programming[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

[b]Functional programming[/b] is a style of programming that (as the name suggests) is based around functions. 
A key part of functional programming is [b]higher-order functions[/b]. Higher-order functions take other functions as arguments, or return them as results.

[s0l0!-header][b]Example:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="py" codeId="381"]def apply_twice(func, arg):
   return func(func(arg))

def add_five(x):
   return x + 5

print(apply_twice(add_five, 10))[/code]
[note]The function [b]apply_twice [/b]takes another function as its argument, and calls it twice inside its body.[/note]

resolved.title: 纯函数
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Pure Functions[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Functional programming seeks to use [b]pure functions[/b]. Pure functions have no side effects, and return a value that depends [b]only [/b]on their arguments.
This is how functions in math work: for example, the [b]cos(x)[/b] will, for the same value of [b]x[/b], always return the same result.
Below are examples of pure and impure functions.

[s0l0!-header][b]Pure function:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="py" ]def pure_function(x, y):
  temp = x + 2*y
  return temp / (2*x + y)[/code]
[s0l0!-header][b]Impure function:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="py" ]some_list = []

def impure(arg):
  some_list.append(arg)[/code]
[note]The function above is not pure, because it changed the state of [b]some_list[/b].[/note]

resolved.title: 纯函数
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Pure Functions[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Using pure functions has both advantages and disadvantages. 
Pure functions are:
- easier to reason about and test.
- more efficient. Once the function has been evaluated for an input, the result can be stored and referred to the next time the function of that input is needed, reducing the number of times the function is called. This is called [b]memoization[/b].
- easier to run in parallel.
[note]Pure functions are more difficult to write in some situations.[/note]

content.text:
使用简单函数既有优点也有缺点：


- 更容易分析和测试。
- 更有效率。一旦函数对某个输入进行了评估，其结果可以被存储起来，并在下次相同输入调用时直接返回结果，从而减少了函数的调用次数。这被称为**记忆**。
- 更容易并行运行。
content.text_html:
Using pure functions has both advantages and disadvantages. Pure functions are:

  • easier to reason about and test.
  • more efficient. Once the function has been evaluated for an input, the result can be stored and referred to the next time the function of that input is needed, reducing the number of times the function is called. This is called memoization.
  • easier to run in parallel.

使用纯函数既有优点也有缺点。 纯函数是。

  • 更容易推理和测试。
  • 更有效率。一旦函数对一个输入进行了评估，其结果可以被存储起来，并在下次需要该输入的函数时被引用，从而减少了函数的调用次数。这被称为记忆。
  • 更容易并行运行。
